Action.description: SCLS 3.1. The specified action; a category-level authorization names the trigger condition that requires a standing evaluation before a specific action proceeds.

category_level.description: True if this is a category-level authorization rather than a specific action.

specification.description: The action stated precisely enough for affected parties to evaluate whether they are materially affected.

trigger_condition.description: SCLS 3.1. Required inside a category-level authorization, naming the condition under which a specific action within the class triggers a standing evaluation.

Action.title: Action

AffectedConstituency.description: SCLS 3.1, 3.1.1. The materially-affected set, identified before the action, on an evidence-and-self-identification basis.

identification_basis.description: SCLS 3.1. Evidence-based where system evidence exists; self-identification permitted.

identified_before_action.description: SCLS 3.1. The identification event precedes execution.

AffectedConstituency.title: AffectedConstituency

Authorization.description: SCLS 3.2, 6.1. A meaningful opportunity to authorize or refuse, the four system obligations, and the response-status distinction.

authorizing_set.description: SCLS 3.2. Neither excludes affected parties nor includes unaffected parties who dilute the affected constituency's voice.

response_status.description: SCLS 3.2. Silence, inaction, and absence of objection are not consent; the system distinguishes authorized, not-yet-responded, and unable-to-respond.

system_obligations.description: SCLS 6.1. The four obligations whose presence makes the opportunity meaningful.

Authorization.title: Authorization

ConformanceAnswer.description: SCLS. Per-invariant answer; silence is not one of the values.
ConformanceAnswer.title: ConformanceAnswer

ConformanceDeclaration.description: SCLS. The invariant conformance answers on the face. There is deliberately no overall or total field: conformance is per-invariant, mirroring the suite's refusal to collapse a profile into a single number and the SLSA Verification-Summary-Attestation shape.
ConformanceDeclaration.title: ConformanceDeclaration

ConsentArchitecture.description: SCLS system-level context. Which domains apply, the adopted tier, the durable constituency definition, the external-override disclosure, and the higher-tier blocks (standing evaluation, detection architecture) that a record declares its context against. The higher-tier blocks are optional in the schema; the checker requires them at the tiers the register specifies.

detection_architecture.description: SCLS 5.3.1. Graduated shadow-dynamics detection. Required by the checker at Instrumented and above.

domains_applicable.description: SCLS 4. The consent domains identified as relevant to the system's operations.

durable_constituency_definition.description: SCLS 3.1.2. Accessible without authority-gating and specific enough for an independent observer to determine participation rights.

external_override_disclosure.description: SCLS 2.3.2. Names the external-legal-override threat, the applicable jurisdictions, and how the gap is addressed.

standing_evaluation.description: SCLS 3.1.1. The four-element standing evaluation mechanism. Required by the checker at Instrumented and above.

ConsentArchitecture.title: ConsentArchitecture

ConsentDomain.description: SCLS 4. The five domains in which consent operates.
ConsentDomain.title: ConsentDomain

ConsentRecord.description: A per-action consent record. Carries the relational predicates and the invariant exposures (Identify, Authorize, Verify) on its face, and declares the system context it was produced under.

action.description: SCLS 3.1. The action being consented to, specified precisely enough to evaluate material effect.

affected_constituency.description: SCLS 3.1. The set identified as materially affected, before the action proceeds.

architecture.description: SCLS system-level context the record declares against.

authorization.description: SCLS 3.2, 6.1. The opportunity to authorize or refuse, the four system obligations, and the response-status distinction.

conformance.description: SCLS. Per-invariant conformance answers on the face; no total.

cost_bearing_party.description: SCLS 2.1. Present when the cost-bearing party is distinct from both the acting and the benefiting party; when present it carries consent to the cost distribution (native nested-required). Whether a distinct cost-bearer exists is domain fact and is checked, not schema-enforced.

domains_touched.description: SCLS 4. Which of the five consent domains this action implicates.

negotiated_limits.description: SCLS 2.3.1. Explicit limits set by the consenting party. Absence in a serving or allowing quadrant is a shadow indicator.

verification.description: SCLS 3.3. The consent record's completeness and durability.

wheel.description: SCLS 2.1, 3.2. The two Wheel axes, both legible to both parties.

withdrawal.description: SCLS 2.3.1. The withdrawal mechanism. Its presence is shape; whether its cost exceeds participation benefit is a checked exit-cost judgment.

ConsentRecord.title: ConsentRecord

CostBearingParty.description: SCLS 2.1. A cost-bearer distinct from the acting and benefiting parties; identified explicitly with consent to the cost distribution obtained before the action.

consent_to_cost_distribution.description: SCLS 2.1. Obtained before the action proceeds (native nested-required).

CostBearingParty.title: CostBearingParty

DetectionArchitecture.description: SCLS 5.3.1. Per shadow type, a graduated detection with a monitoring and an escalation threshold; flags for Signal Escalation, never adjudicates.

transparent_to_participants.description: SCLS 5.3.1. The monitored patterns are transparent to participants (itself an Observation-domain consent requirement).

DetectionArchitecture.title: DetectionArchitecture

DurableConstituencyDefinition.description: SCLS 3.1.2. The durable, accessible definition of who holds participation rights.

independent_observer_determinable.description: Specific enough that an independent observer can determine whether a party holds participation rights without the author's intent.

DurableConstituencyDefinition.title: DurableConstituencyDefinition

ExternalOverrideDisclosure.description: SCLS 2.3.2. The disclosure whose absence is a consent legibility failure.

gap_treatment.description: How the gap between explicit consent and externally imposed obligations is addressed. Presence is shape; adequacy is checked.

jurisdictions.description: The external legal jurisdictions that apply.

ExternalOverrideDisclosure.title: ExternalOverrideDisclosure

limit.description: An explicit boundary set by the consenting party.

ResponseStatus.description: SCLS 3.2. The distinction silence cannot collapse.
ResponseStatus.title: ResponseStatus

ShadowDetection.description: SCLS 5.3.1. One shadow type's graduated detection.

escalation_threshold.description: The signal or combination that triggers Signal Escalation.

ShadowDetection.title: ShadowDetection

ShadowType.description: SCLS 5.3.1. The shadow dynamics with detection signatures.
ShadowType.title: ShadowType

StandingEvaluation.description: SCLS 3.1.1. The four elements, none concentrated in a single actor.

distributed_evaluation.description: The evaluation function is not concentrated in a single actor.

StandingEvaluation.title: StandingEvaluation

SystemObligations.description: SCLS 6.1. The four obligations are on the system, not the participant. Presence is shape; the qualitative reads (is the description evaluable, is the exit cost punitive) are checked.

exit_or_objection_cost_not_punitive.description: SCLS 6.1. The structural cost of dissent is recorded; whether it is punitive is a checked judgment.

legibility.description: SCLS 6.1. The action described in terms the constituency can evaluate.

support.description: SCLS 6.1. Analytical infrastructure to evaluate implications.

time.description: SCLS 6.1. A consent window proportional to complexity (Section 6.4).

SystemObligations.title: SystemObligations

Verification.description: SCLS 3.3. The consent record's completeness and durability.

tamper_evident.description: SCLS 3.3. The record is tamper-evident (the ASEP durable-logging requirement).

Verification.title: Verification

WheelAxes.description: SCLS 2.1, 3.2. The two independent axes, both legible to both parties (2.3.1 bidirectional awareness).

both_legible_to_both_parties.description: SCLS 2.3.1. Both axes were legible to both parties at the time of the interaction.

who_acts.description: The action axis. Who is acting.

who_benefits.description: The benefit axis. Who the action is for.

WheelAxes.title: WheelAxes

Withdrawal.description: SCLS 2.3.1. Revocability. Structurally feasible, not merely formally permitted.

mechanism.description: The mechanism by which consent can be withdrawn.

structural_cost.description: The structural cost of withdrawing. Whether it exceeds participation benefit is a checked judgment.

Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal
